tb21_profile.skill: Reverse-engineer a binary executable (strings/objdump/gdb/black-box), locate and exploit a vulnerability (buffer overflow) to bypass an auth/validation check, and recover an embedded FLAG{...} secret
tb21_profile.domain: Binary/ELF reversing and memory-corruption exploitation; Linux security, authentication tokens and hidden secrets
tb21_profile.task_form: reverse-engineer-a-binary + exploit-a-vulnerability to extract a secret and write it to a result file

notes: Strong retrieval for this task. TMax, TerminalWorld and Recursive-Task-Synthesis all contain genuine binary-reversing and buffer-overflow-exploitation tasks, so the honest top10 draws from all three; SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench have essentially no exploitation content. The single closest SWE-Rebench candidate is ctfd-432 (a real access-control/auth-bypass vulnerability); pfp (binary-template parser) tasks are the best binary-format-reasoning proxies there, and cantools serves the same role in SWE-Smith - all capped at overall 2-4 because they are library bug fixes, not reverse-and-exploit tasks. Lexical false positives I demoted: many TMax and TW hits merely mention auth/tokens but are log-forensics, JWT-web, or pcap analysis with no binary reversing; the SWE 'secret'/'token' hits are cloud-mock plumbing. Note RTS/TW have many near-duplicate Protostar-stack3 and crackme variants - I kept only diverse representatives to avoid burning slots on clones.
